newsitem.title: UK: Brady bond trade capped ahead of U.S. data-dealers.
newsitem.headline: Brady bond trade capped ahead of U.S. data-dealers.

text.p: Cautiousness ahead of U.S. data capped trade in a quiet Brady market on Tuesday but expectations were for further gains in the U.S. Treasury market following the data release, dealers said.
Consumer prices, Housing Starts and Industrial production for May are among the U.S. indicators due for release on Tuesday.
BankAmerica analyst Richard Gray said the data was likely to be "friendly".
"We expect further gains in the Treasury market and further spread tightening in Bradies," he said.
Gray said Brazil still had upside potential.
"They had some quite good numbers (on Monday) in terms of current account and the recovery in the foreign exchange reserves," he said.
Figures released this week show Brazilian industrial activity and jobs growth are at their best levels in two years.
At 0830 GMT Brazil DISC Z BRFLTD24=RR were bid at 84.625, Brazil IDUS BRFLA01=RR at 98.625, BRAZIL "C" BR8D14=RR at 81.625 and BRAZIL PAR BR4D24=RR at 68.875.
Dealers said they were also awaiting launch of Russia's second dollar deal -- expected to be launched on Thursday.

Russia's next Eurobond is likely to have a 10-year maturity and be for at least $1.0 billion. Bankers said a 10-year Russian Eurobond could be priced to yield around 375 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes.
